stem.en: Mauna Kea in Hawai‘i is said to be taller than Mount Everest, yet Everest is called the highest mountain. How can both be true?

text.en: The Mauna Kea figure is simply a mistake

feedback.en: No. Mauna Kea is about 10,000 m tall from its base on the sea floor.

text.en: The two are measured from different places

feedback.en: Yes. Everest is measured from sea level, and Mauna Kea from its base on the sea floor.

text.en: The sea floor lies higher than the plains of Asia

feedback.en: No. The sea floor near Hawai‘i lies far below sea level.

text.en: Mauna Kea stands nearer to the centre of the Earth

feedback.en: No. That has nothing to do with how a mountain is measured.

explanation.en: A height depends on where you measure from. Everest is 8,849 m above sea level. Mauna Kea is about 4,200 m above sea level, but about 10,000 m from its base on the sea floor.

hints.en: Ask where the bottom of each mountain is.
